reason: Cliopatria labels Alexander's conquests 'Ptolemaic Kingdom' from 331 BCE. Ptolemy became satrap of Egypt only in 323 and king in 305, so the label is 8-26 years early. The two affected records are the conquered territories: -331..-327 (1.22M km2, Anatolia/Levant/Egypt) and -326..-324 (4.83M km2, the whole empire to the Indus), while 'Macedonian Empire' in the same years is only the 218k km2 homeland. From -323 Cliopatria self-corrects: Macedonian Empire becomes 4.70M km2 and Ptolemaic Kingdom disappears until -307.
effect: Both records render as Macedonian Empire, so Alexander's realm reads as one polity in one colour. Homeland and conquests remain separate features, which is correct - they were administered differently.
evidence: AWMC alexanders_empire extent agrees with the renamed geometry at IoU 0.79 and 0.76 - an independent tier-1 source confirming the rename

reason: Cliopatria carries umbrella records that duplicate the geometry of the entities they contain rather than adding territory - e.g. '(Phoenician Empire)' has Components='Phoenicia' and exactly Phoenicia's 35130 km2; '(Macedonian Empire)' duplicates Macedonian Empire's 218048 km2. Rendering both double-draws the same ground and doubles the label. The test is exact: in all 13765 records, a non-empty Components field occurs iff the name is parenthesised (1722 of 1722, and 0 non-parenthesised records have components).
effect: 1722 of 13765 features suppressed. Revisit when the polity ontology lands - these wrappers are the raw material for the sovereign/sub-polity hierarchy and should eventually become hierarchy edges rather than be dropped.
correction: This decision originally scoped on Type=='RELATION', which caught only 385 of the 1722 wrappers - the other 1337 are typed POLITY despite being wrappers. Parenthesised name and RELATION type are not the same set.
evidence: parenthesised names 1722, of which POLITY 1337 and RELATION 385
